name: Walking with a Smile
description: Supporting trauma recovery and healing. Resources to help you move from survival to living, at your own pace.

identity.tagline: Step Into a Life Beyond Trauma
identity.mission: Our mission at Walking With A Smile is to guide trauma survivors in shifting from pain-centered living to authentic self-ownership. Through compassionate advice, actionable resources, and a supportive community, we aim to open doors for individuals to rediscover joy, reclaim their power, and step confidently into a future no longer defined by past experiences.
identity.vision: Our vision at Walking With A Smile is to create a world where every trauma survivor has the tools and support needed to heal, grow, and confidently embrace a renewed sense of hope through effective communication practices. We envision a community that fosters compassion, empowerment, and resilience, where individuals can transform adversity into progress and rebuild their lives with strength and positivity.
identity.brandStory: I spent most of my life thinking that constant stress, fear, and anxiety were just part of who I was. The weight of trauma felt like something I'd carry forever. Then one day, I got tired of it. I started pushing back. Slowly. Messily. Not perfectly. And something shifted. When I finally stopped letting trauma be the first thing I introduced about myself, the whole world got bigger. I found out I actually liked who I was underneath all that weight. I could breathe. I could be curious about life instead of just bracing for it. That's when I knew I wanted to create something for other people who might be ready for the same shift. Because everyone deserves to feel lighter. Everyone deserves to walk with a smile.

audience.primary: Trauma survivors and individuals seeking personal growth post-trauma
audience.demographics: Age 25-55, predominantly female but open to all genders, high school diploma or higher, middle to upper-middle class
painPoints: Constant stress and anxiety from past trauma
Lack of accessible, practical healing resources
Feeling isolated in their recovery journey

themes: Moving from trauma-centered to self-centered living
pillars: You first - reconnecting with yourself beyond trauma
contentGuidelines.ctaStyle: Gentle invitation with agency and choice, not pressure (e.g., 'Explore Resources', 'Start Your Journey', 'Begin Your Transformation')

colors.summary: Our color palette reflects calm, warmth, and gentle hope. Soft neutrals (warm beige, light grays) create a comforting foundation, while gentle pastels (sage green primary, dusty coral secondary, soft blues and mauves) add subtle, uplifting accents. These colors evoke safety, peace, and possibility without overwhelming.
colors.do: Use primary sage green for main actions and emphasis. Use secondary coral for warmth and secondary CTAs. Maintain soft, low-contrast combinations for accessibility and comfort. Use pastels to highlight without jarring. Ensure sufficient contrast for text readability (4.5:1 minimum).
colors.dont: Avoid bright, aggressive colors that might trigger anxiety. Don't use high-contrast or neon shades. Avoid pure black text on white backgrounds—use softer grays. Don't use red for anything beyond system states (errors).

fonts.summary: Quicksand is our single font family, used consistently across all brand touchpoints. Its rounded, friendly letterforms create approachability while remaining professional. The geometric yet soft structure communicates both clarity and warmth.
fonts.do: Use medium weight (500) for body text for better readability. Use semibold (600) for headings. Maintain wide letter-spacing (0.05em) on headings for openness. Use generous line-height (1.625) for body text to aid readability and reduce cognitive load.
fonts.dont: Don't use multiple font families—consistency is key to brand recognition. Avoid light weights below 400 for accessibility. Don't use all-caps extensively. Don't reduce letter-spacing on headings.

logos.summary: Our logo represents warmth, approachability, and forward movement. It should always have breathing room and be placed on appropriate backgrounds.
logos.do: Maintain clear space around the logo. Use on light, neutral backgrounds for best visibility. Ensure logo remains legible at all sizes. Use the provided variations (nav, favicon, SEO) for their intended purposes.
logos.dont: Don't place logo on busy backgrounds or competing imagery. Don't stretch, skew, or alter proportions. Don't use colors other than provided versions. Don't place on backgrounds with insufficient contrast.

brandVoice.summary: Our voice is uplifting, supportive, and empowering—meeting people where they are while gently guiding them toward who they can become. We speak with genuine warmth, never clinical detachment or toxic positivity. Every message reinforces personal agency and hope.
brandVoice.do: Use second person ('you', 'your') to create connection. Lead with empowerment and possibility. Acknowledge struggle without dwelling on it. Offer tools and options, not prescriptions. Celebrate small progress. Use active voice and encouraging language.
brandVoice.dont: Don't use clinical jargon or therapy-speak. Avoid toxic positivity or minimizing pain. Don't tell people how they 'should' feel or heal. Avoid dramatic or救援-focused language. Don't speak in absolutes or timelines.

photos.summary: Imagery should evoke calm, hope, and gentle progress. Use soft, natural scenes, subtle symbolism of growth and transformation (budding plants, sunrise), and inclusive representations of healing and peace.
photos.do: Use soft, natural lighting. Choose images with muted, pastel tones that match the color palette. Include nature imagery (gentle landscapes, plants, water, sunrise). Show peaceful, contemplative moments. Ensure imagery is inclusive and diverse.
photos.dont: Avoid dark, dramatic, or distressing imagery. Don't use stock photos with forced smiles or unrealistic happiness. Avoid clinical settings or medical imagery. Don't use images with harsh lighting or saturated colors.

graphics.summary: Graphics and illustrations should be minimalist, soft, and organic. Use gentle curves, rounded corners, and flowing shapes that feel approachable and non-threatening.
graphics.do: Use rounded corners and soft edges. Maintain ample white space. Use subtle shadows and soft glows. Create organic, flowing shapes. Keep designs minimalist and uncluttered.
graphics.dont: Avoid sharp angles and aggressive geometric shapes. Don't overcrowd designs with multiple elements. Avoid complex patterns that create visual noise. Don't use heavy, dark borders.

icons.summary: Icons should be simple, rounded, and friendly. They serve as gentle visual cues without overwhelming the content.
icons.do: Use rounded, outlined icon styles. Maintain consistent stroke width. Use primary or accent colors sparingly. Ensure icons are universally recognizable. Size appropriately for context.
icons.dont: Don't use filled/solid icons extensively. Avoid overly complex or detailed icons. Don't mix icon styles (outlined with filled). Avoid using icons as decoration without purpose.

brandIntention.summary: Walking with a Smile empowers trauma survivors to break free from a life defined by past wounds, shifting their focus from trauma to self-directed fulfillment. By providing practical information, empathetic support, and user-friendly resources, we guide individuals to embrace change, reclaim control, and cultivate the capacity for more joyful, meaningful experiences.
brandIntention.keywords: empowerment, transformation, resilience, hope, authentic living, trauma recovery, self-ownership

promptConfig.snippetShort: Walking with a Smile: Empowering trauma survivors through practical healing resources, compassionate support, and community. Gentle, hopeful voice. Sage green/coral palette. Focus on self-ownership and transformation.
promptConfig.snippetLong: Walking with a Smile is a trauma recovery platform dedicated to helping survivors shift from pain-centered living to authentic self-ownership. Through practical worksheets, workbooks, guides, blog content, and community support, we provide accessible tools for healing and growth. Our brand voice is uplifting, supportive, and future-focused—meeting people where they are while guiding them toward who they can become. Design uses soft neutrals (warm beige #f9f8f6) with gentle pastels (sage green #8fa68a primary, dusty coral #c4907c secondary). Typography is Quicksand for all text, creating warmth and approachability. Core values: Empowerment, Authenticity, Resilience, Hope, Kindness. Target audience: Trauma survivors age 25-55 seeking practical healing resources and community.
